questions.q: Why does this lesson say a vendor's clean intake assessment effectively has an expiration date?
options: Because SIG and CAIQ questionnaires are legally valid for only 90 days under industry regulation
Because the vendor is required to delete its own completed questionnaire after one year
Because intake assessments are always inaccurate even on the day they are completed
Because a vendor's security posture changes continuously — staff turnover, infrastructure migration, rushed features, and acquisitions none of which show up in a questionnaire filed months earlier
questions.explain: A vendor's security posture isn't a fixed property measured once. Staff turnover, infrastructure changes, deadline-pressured shortcuts, and acquisitions can all change the real risk without ever appearing in an old assessment.

questions.q: How should the cadence for periodic vendor reassessment be determined, according to this lesson?
options: Every vendor should be reassessed on the exact same fixed calendar schedule regardless of risk
Tied to the vendor's risk tier — Tier 1 vendors reassessed most often, lower tiers less often or only when triggered
Reassessment should only happen if the vendor requests it
Reassessment cadence is set entirely by the vendor, never the customer
questions.explain: Reassessment cadence mirrors the same risk-based logic as initial tiering: the highest-risk vendors get checked most often, rather than applying one uniform schedule regardless of actual risk.

questions.q: What do security rating services provide that periodic reassessment alone does not?
options: A continuous, externally observable score of a vendor's security posture between scheduled assessment cycles
A legally binding guarantee that the vendor will never suffer a breach
A replacement for all contractual security requirements covered in the previous lesson
A one-time certification that never needs to be checked again
questions.explain: Security rating services continuously scan externally observable signals (exposed services, outdated software, leaked credentials, and more) to produce a score, giving an early warning signal between the less frequent formal reassessments.

questions.q: What is the purpose of breach notification monitoring, as distinct from the contractual notification requirement itself?
options: It eliminates the need for any contractual breach notification clause
It is only relevant for Tier 3, low-risk vendors

It closes the gap between a vendor being contractually obligated to report an incident and actually confirming the vendor reported it in time, including watching external sources for undisclosed incidents
It requires the customer to personally investigate every vendor's internal network after signing a contract
questions.explain: A contract creates the obligation to notify within a defined window; monitoring is the active process of tracking whether that obligation was actually met and watching for incidents a vendor hasn't yet reported.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed in this lesson as an event that should trigger an off-cycle vendor reassessment, outside the normal review schedule?
options: The vendor being acquired by or merging with another company
The vendor renewing its office lease
The vendor changing its company logo
The vendor hiring a new marketing intern
questions.explain: An acquisition or merger can materially change a vendor's security posture, infrastructure, and staff overnight, which is exactly the kind of event that should pull a reassessment forward regardless of the normal cadence.
